reasoning: The 2026 FIFA World Cup will be held in North America. Historically, only 8 countries have won: Uruguay, Italy, Germany, Brazil, England, Argentina, France, and Spain. For a first-time winner to emerge, one of the other ~200 FIFA nations must win. While unlikely, the expanded 48-team format and North American venue could favor teams like Mexico, USA, or Canada. However, traditional powerhouses remain heavily favored. Based on historical patterns where first-time winners are rare (only 2 in last 40 years: Greece 2004 Euros, but no World Cup first-timers since 1978), the probability of a first-time World Cup winner is low but non-negligible.
